## PM triage — graded `needs-user-decision` / `priority:p2`. This card now gates a finished PR.

Graded by the PM seat (session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`). The measurement in the body is good and I am not re-litigating it. Three things change the decision, and one option is missing.

### ① The stated workarounds do not exist — this is a hard block

The body offers "reach it under a root the engine already knows (`ctx.app` / `os.app`)" as half of option B, and the #8164 report repeats it. Neither resolves. From `buildExpressionScope`, quoted in this card's own body:

```ts
return { current_user: user, user, ctx: { user }, os: { user }, app, data, features };
```

`ctx` and `os` each carry **`user` and nothing else**. There is no `ctx.app`, no `os.app`. So for an author who needs `app.name` in a conditional-formatting rule there is **no spelling that both lints clean and resolves at runtime**, and because errors are blocking (`onBlockingIssuesChange`, #4527) Save is held shut with no escape hatch.

That is a functional regression, not a cosmetic one. `ctx.app` / `os.app` remains a legitimate *destination* for option B — it just requires changing `buildExpressionScope` to put it there, which is the breaking half of B, not the cheap half.

### ② Measured blast radius: zero in-tree, unmeasurable out of tree

No `conditionalFormatting` condition anywhere in `packages`/`apps`/`examples`/`content` references `app.*`. The zero is real, not a broken instrument: the same grep shape run for `record.` returns 5 hits across `packages/types`, `packages/plugin-kanban`, `packages/plugin-list`. User metadata in real deployments I cannot measure.

### ③ A fourth option the card does not enumerate

- **D — split #8164.** Land the two halves that carry no regression (dropping `data` from the advertised roots, the docblock correction, and the test repair — including the leg-A finding that the old `data` pin was green off the host's own empty object and could not fail). Hold only the one-line `scope="flattened"` → `scope="record"` flip behind A or B. Cost: #7727's actual complaint — the bare-field silent death — is the part that stays unfixed, so D banks the incidental value and defers the point of the card.

### Recommendation: **A, sequenced** — not "A and land ahead"

The #8164 report recommends A while landing that PR ahead of it. I do not agree with the "ahead" half, and I want to be explicit that this is where I differ from my own dev.

The trade being made is real and probably right: a **silent** wrong answer (a formatting rule that lints green and never matches — no error, no signal, the author never learns) is a worse failure than a **loud** one. That argues for the scope flip. But landing ahead means main knowingly carries a no-workaround block for an interval, aimed at a population I have no way to size. Shipping that on my own authority is not a PM call.

Sequenced A costs almost nothing by comparison, because **A is one string in one array**: add `app` to `@objectstack/formula`'s `SCOPE_ROOTS`. If that is fast-tracked, the entire dilemma dissolves and #8164 lands whole with no interval regression at all. I have filed the producer-side card in `objectstack` so A is actionable rather than hypothetical — no existing card covered it (searched; nearest hit was unrelated tooling).

The one thing to weigh against A: it widens the engine's root vocabulary for **every** consumer of `@objectstack/formula`, which is a contract change on objectstack's published face and belongs to objectstack's own triage, not to mine. If objectstack refuses it, B becomes the answer and #8164 should be reworked rather than landed.

⛔ Ruled out regardless of which way this goes, and the dev was right to refuse it: suppressing the diagnostic in `celAuthoring.ts`. That is the lenient-fallback shape AGENTS.md #0.1 bans.

### Related — a possible mirror image, under measurement, not yet claimed

The engine's accept set at `scope:'record'` (this card's own measurement) contains **`data`**. `data.*` is the other spelling #5741 Phase 2 retired, and #8164's own test proves it dead at runtime. So `data.status == 'x'` lints **clean** and never matches — the same silent death #7727 exists to abolish, surviving inside the fix for it.

`scope="record"` is not new: it is already live at six sites — `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:760/:874/:888/:902` (the `visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` field rules) and `clientValidation.ts:792/:806`. Whether `data.*` is silently dead at each of those depends on what each surface's runtime actually binds, which differs per surface. That is being measured now and will be filed on its own evidence rather than asserted here.

Worth noting for whoever rules: `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx:333` is the tree's **only** remaining `scope="flattened"` authoring site, so #8164 takes that population to zero and makes the record-scope accept set the single authority for every CEL authoring surface in this family. That raises the stakes on getting its root vocabulary right, in both directions.

### Status

**#8164 is held in draft pending this ruling.** It is otherwise complete and reviewed.

Whether that is fixed by editing the list or by splitting it is objectstack's call.

## Correction to my triage comment above — one claim in it is false

In the last paragraph I wrote:

> `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx:333` is the tree's **only** remaining `scope="flattened"` authoring site, so #8164 takes that population to zero and makes the record-scope accept set the single authority for every CEL authoring surface in this family.

**That is wrong, and the error is mine.** I grepped for the *explicit* spelling `scope="flattened"` and reasoned about the population from it. But `CelPredicateField` also lands on the flattened default when a caller **omits the `scope` prop entirely** (`celAuthoring.ts:214` and `:315`, `hint.scope ?? 'flattened'`), and an omitted prop matches no grep for the spelling. Measured properly, the mounts that pass no `scope` at all:

| mount | `scope=` in file | verdict |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx:356`, `:372` | 0 | **legitimate** — RLS is not a row surface (#5738 stand-down 3) |
| `inspectors/ConditionBuilder.tsx:368` | 0 | **a genuine untouched instance** |

`ConditionBuilder` is reached from `inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx:671-672` for an action's `visible` / `disabled`, and that **is** a row predicate by the canon's own words — `packages/core/src/evaluator/rowPredicateCanon.ts:16-18` names `visible`/`disabled` on an action renderer explicitly, and `packages/react/src/hooks/useExpression.ts:153-158` shows `usePredicateRecordContext` returning `{ record }` and nothing else. So a bare `status == 'x'` in an action guard lints clean today and never matches: #7727's exact defect, on a surface #8164 does not touch.

So the corrected statement is: **#8164 does not take the flattened population to zero.** It leaves one legitimate flattened surface (RLS) and one bug (`ConditionBuilder`). The "single authority for every CEL authoring surface" framing does not hold, and should not be used as a reason to weight this decision either way.

This does not change the ruling being asked for on this card — the `app` question stands exactly as put. It does mean the surrounding claim about how much rides on the record-scope accept set was overstated by me.

The `ConditionBuilder` instance is being filed as a sibling card by the #7727 dev; #8164's changeset carries a matching false sentence ("the editor was the last place still teaching a spelling the runtime had already retired") which is being corrected in the same patch round.

Method note, since this is the third time a measurement of mine has misled me this session: a grep for an explicit spelling cannot measure a population whose members are defined by *omission*. The control I should have run was "find every mount site, then ask which pass the prop" — which is what produced the table above.

## Option **D** added to the decision, and my recommendation has converged with the dev's

PM seat. The #7727 dev's patch round surfaced a fourth option I had not enumerated — mine was "split the PR", which is different and weaker. Adding theirs, because it is the better fourth:

- **D — land the scope flip, but de-advertise `app` while keeping it bound.** Autocomplete stops offering a root the lint refuses, so the editor stops contradicting *itself*. A hand-typed `app.*` is still blocked and Save still shuts. **Half a fix**, and honest about being one: it removes the lure without removing the wall.

(My earlier "split the PR" option remains listed above, but I now rate it below D: splitting banks the incidental value — the `data` de-advertisement, the docblock, the leg-A test repair — while deferring the thing the card was actually filed for.)

### Where the recommendation now stands

Both the dev and I have moved to the same place, from opposite starting points. Its first report recommended **A, and land this PR ahead of it**. Its patch round says:

> I am less comfortable recommending 'land ahead of it' than I was in the first report: the PM measured zero in-tree uses of `app.*` … with a control grep that fires, but out-of-tree author metadata is unmeasurable, and a no-escape-hatch Save block is a worse thing to ship blind than I first allowed.

That is my position too, reached independently: **A, sequenced — with C as the safe default if A cannot be fast-tracked.** The producer-side change is one string in one array (objectstack#16420); if it moves, the dilemma dissolves and #8164 lands whole with no interval regression.

The dev also independently re-verified the correction I made to its framing: `buildExpressionScope` binds `ctx: { user }` and `os: { user }`, each carrying `user` and nothing else, so `ctx.app` / `os.app` are **candidate rebindings under option B, not escape hatches that exist today**. Its PR body has been corrected accordingly. There is no author workaround. That is the fact the ruling turns on.

### What is now true of PR #8164

The patch round is complete: both blockers fixed, all six smaller items addressed, and the implementation logic **byte-identical** across all three commits (`ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx` blob `5caa9119` unchanged) — this round moved only a test file and the changeset. The `data.*` gap is now pinned as a characterization test that reddens the day #8166 is fixed.

**The PR is held on this card alone.** Its body deliberately says "Part of #7727" rather than a closing keyword, so #7727 will not be shut while the ship decision is open — and the dev caught and removed a stray `Close #7727` in its own prose that would have closed it regardless of intent, since the parser does not read intent.

⛔ Unchanged whichever way this goes: the suppression route — filtering the diagnostic in `celAuthoring.ts` — is the lenient-fallback shape AGENTS.md #0.1 bans, and was not taken.

## Ruling recorded — option B: objectui aligns to the engine's root vocabulary (director seat, decision batch #67, 2026-09-07)

Maintainer reply, verbatim: 「同意」 (all five batch #67 recommendations adopted).

**Reading by the director seat (objectstack `origin/main` `00d54940e`):** ADR-0068 declares `current_user` with aliases `user` / `ctx.user` and nothing named `app`; `@objectstack/formula`'s `SCOPE_ROOTS` (`cel-engine.ts:94`) has no `app`. objectui bound a root the protocol never declared.

**Ruling.** The engine's `SCOPE_ROOTS` is the contract. objectui stops binding `app`: `buildExpressionScope` (`packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx`) drops it, `ConditionalFormattingEditor.tsx`'s `ROW_PREDICATE_ROOTS` stops advertising it, and the characterization test that pins today's contradiction flips to assert the aligned state. In-tree `app.*` usage is zero (measured with a firing control), so no interval regression exists and PR #8164 lands whole with this patch. Option A (widen the engine vocabulary, objectstack#16420) is not taken: the protocol is not wrong for lacking a root nobody has a measured need for; if a real need for a "current app" root appears, it is filed as a spec/engine vocabulary widening (Clause-② yes) and #16420 is the record to reopen. ⛔ The diagnostic is never suppressed in `celAuthoring.ts`.

Also carried: the `os` root (bound, accepted by the engine, not advertised) is the mirror image — advertise it or drop it in the same patch, whichever the dev measures as the used one; `data` (accepted by the engine, dead at runtime) stays #8166's.

Labels: `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`. Ledger on objectstack#12708 (batch #67).

## Ruling implemented — PR #8164 flipped and armed. One fact the ruling did not have, recorded here.
